about indéva

it started on a building site.

arpit saini grew up watching buildings go up. his family has been in construction since 1939, from his grandfather's brick business to his father's sites. on those sites he saw the same story again and again: a beautiful drawing, a contractor guessing how to build it, and a homeowner stuck in the middle. indéva studio was started to end the guessing. the people who design your home are the people who build it, and they answer for every detail until it is done.

01
one team, start to finish

the people who draw your home are the people who build it. you will never hear "that's the contractor's problem."

02
the plan comes first

light, movement and storage are solved before we talk finishes. a pretty room with a bad plan is still a bad room.

03
made for your room, not a catalogue

beds, wardrobes and joinery are designed in-house and built to fit your walls, not squeezed in from a showroom.

04
the real number, upfront

an itemised estimate before work begins, so you approve every rupee instead of discovering it halfway through.

founder
arpit saini
founder & ceo, indéva studio
Built on generations of understanding how things are made.

arpit saini grew up around construction. his grandfather was involved in building and the family brick business, a legacy dating back to 1939, and his father carried it forward through construction.

those years on sites taught him that an idea has little value if it cannot be built properly. he founded indéva studio to bring design and execution closer together, so every decision accounts for budgets, materials, craftsmanship, timelines and real site conditions.

"impact over hard work. nobody lives in the hours we put in. they live in what we built."

director
veenu saini
director of projects & compliance, indéva studio
Where design meets accountability.

veenu saini brings 25+ years of experience in manufacturing, sales, operations, financial compliance and site audits with quality control checks.

at indéva studio he oversees project delivery and compliance, keeping timelines, vendor commitments, documentation and site quality on track so that what is designed on paper is delivered on site exactly as promised.

his years on factory floors and in audits shape a simple discipline: every material checked, every stage inspected and every rupee accounted for before a home is handed over.

"design inspires. discipline delivers."

our philosophy

five pillars

pillar 01
the invisible detail

true luxury is felt, not seen. we obsess over elements you don't notice until they're missing — the silent glide of a drawer, the tactile weight of a door handle, the acoustic warmth of a well-layered room. invisible engineering is the foundation that lets the aesthetic feel effortless.

pillar 02
the art of the mix

we reject the total look of a single era or brand. we pair sleek modern industrialism with the warmth of an antique. this juxtaposition creates a dialogue that prevents a space from feeling dated and allows it to remain timeless through its eclectic soul.

pillar 03
imperfection as character

a room that is too perfect is a room without character. we leave space for the happy accident — books slightly off-centre, a weathered patina, a rug with a softened edge. this quiet imperfection invites people to relax, not retreat.

pillar 04
confidence over rules

design rules are references, not commandments. we break them when a space asks us to — mixing patterns, shifting scale, placing art where it feels right. this confidence ensures the result is not a copy of a magazine, but an original expression of identity.

pillar 05
human-centricity first

design is a service to the soul, not just an aesthetic exercise. we prioritize habitability before selecting a colour palette. we map morning light, the flow of conversation, and the physical comfort of a seated guest. a chair is only beautiful if it invites you to stay.

how we work

the project
journey.

design with clarity. deliver with confidence.

01
stage one
enquiry
project basics reviewed

initial contact to review the project at a high level — scope, site, typology, and intent. we assess fit before committing time.

we ask difficult questions early.
because late surprises are expensive.
02
stage two
alignment
brief, budget & intent set

before aesthetics, we establish clarity. brief, budget, site realities, constraints — all discussed openly. roles and responsibilities locked.

03
stage three
onboarding
scope, roles & timelines locked

formal engagement begins. scope of work defined in writing. team roles confirmed. project timeline agreed. no ambiguity about who is responsible for what.

focused direction.
disciplined process.
flawless handover.
04
stage four
design
layouts, concept & furniture

spatial planning, concept development, furniture logic, material language, lighting strategy — all developed as a coherent system. 3d visualization used for proportion validation and client alignment before build.

05
stage five
execution
drawings, site control & coordination

detailed working drawings, joinery detailing, electrical coordination, ceiling plans, wall elevations. vendor alignment, regular site reviews, design protection during build.

we draw for contractors,
not for applause.
06
stage six
handover
final checks & delivery

final quality review against design intent. snagging completed. space handed over only when the standard is met — not before. we don't disappear after drawings. we stay until it's right.

what gets built is the only truth.
